```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

The `curequantile` package can be used to fit quantile regression model for 
censored time-to-event data with a cure fraction.

To illustrate the functionality of the `curequantile` package, we first load the 
necessary libraries and the `breast_data` dataset. The data consist of 462 women 
from county code 175 (Union of Iowa, Morgan of Kentucky, and Laurens of Georgia) 
diagnosed with localized or regional breast cancer between 2004 and 2017, 
extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database.

```{r setup}
library(curequantile)
library(survival)
library(maxLik)
data("breast_data")
head(breast_data)
```

A cure quantile regression model can be fit using the `curequantile` function.

```{r example}
fit_breast <- curequantile(Surv(log(Time), Delta) ~ Age + Size,
  data = breast_data, subset = 1:200)
```

The `coef()` function extracts the parameter estimates at a specific quantile 
`tau`. 

```{r coef}
coefficients <- coef(fit_breast, tau = 0.50)
names(coefficients)
coefficients$gamma_est
coefficients$beta_est
```

Here, `gamma_est` contains the incidence parameter estimates, while `beta_est` 
contains the latency parameter estimates at the specified quantile, `tau`. 
Finally, `eta_est` gives the conditional probabilities of being susceptible, and 
therefore has a length equal to the number of rows in the input data frame.

Alternatively, `print()` prints the coefficients at the user-specified quantile
`tau` to the console.

```{r print}
print(fit_breast, tau = 0.50)
```

The `summary()` function returns the parameter estimates, bootstrap standard 
errors, $Z$-test statistics, $p$-values, and bootstrap confidence intervals for 
both the incidence covariates and the latency covariates at the specified 
quantile, `tau`. For computational speed, this vignette uses `b = 5` bootstrap 
resamples, whereas the function defaults to `b = 200`.

```{r summary}
summary <- summary(fit_breast, tau = 0.50, b = 5)
```

The `plot()` function displays the quantile parameter estimates for latency and 
their corresponding confidence intervals for each covariate across the 
user-specified range of `tau`. For illustration, only b = 10 bootstrap 
resamples are used here.

```{r plot}
plot(fit_breast, tau = seq(0.25, 0.75, by = 0.25), b = 10, seed = 2)
```

Additional S3 methods available for `curequantile` objects include:

- `dim()`: Returns the number of observations along with the number of incidence and latency covariates.
- `formula()`: Extracts the model formula.
- `logLik()`: Returns the log-likelihood of the fitted model.
- `nobs()`: Returns the number of observations used to fit the model.
- `predict()`: Generates predictions from the fitted model.
